baseline.unit: Average annual dollars per BLS consumer unit, not median or per-person
baseline.scopeNotes: Average national spending by consumer units, not local ZIP prices. BLS survey was weighted to address an October–November 2025 data-collection interruption. Changes in spending reflect prices, quantities, and mix. BLS housing includes utilities; never add a utilities line to housing.

categories.label: Housing
categories.coverage: Housing spending includes shelter, utilities, furnishings and operations, not a typical rent or mortgage quote.
categories.mechanism: Rents may be shaped by landlord and software practices; utility networks are regulated natural-monopoly structures. Local supply, rates and taxes also matter.
categories.whatBenefits: Property owners and franchise utilities may gain pricing or service-territory advantages, depending on rules and market conditions.
categories.whoPays: Renters and ratepayers may face reduced alternatives, but no verified typical dollar overcharge is available.
categories.unresolved: No substantiated nationwide concentration-attributable housing premium or ZIP-specific landlord/utility competition map.

categories.label: Transportation
categories.coverage: All BLS transportation spending; not just airfare, tolls or transit fares.
categories.mechanism: Competition among airline routes can change ticket prices. Auto costs, fuel, toll policy and transit investment are separate drivers.
categories.whatBenefits: A carrier with fewer route competitors may retain higher fares, but cost structures and operational efficiencies also matter.
categories.whoPays: Passengers on affected routes can pay more when competition falls; the broad transportation average does not measure the airline effect.
categories.unresolved: No national fraction of transportation spending attributable to route concentration; geographic route- and fare-level comparisons required.

categories.label: Groceries at home
categories.coverage: Food purchased for home consumption only. This is a subset of BLS total food spending ($10,633); excludes restaurants.
categories.mechanism: Concentrated meatpacking buyers can have leverage over cattle producers, but retail shelf prices reflect processing, logistics and retailer decisions too.
categories.whatBenefits: Large processors may gain purchasing leverage and scale; efficiency may or may not pass through to retailers or shoppers.
categories.whoPays: Independent ranchers may receive lower bids; the effect on grocery customers is unresolved.
categories.unresolved: No verified consumer grocery premium derived from four-packer procurement concentration; farmgate-versus-retail causal link not established.

categories.label: Healthcare
categories.coverage: Direct consumer-unit healthcare outlays, not the country's total national health expenditure and not all employer-paid costs.
categories.mechanism: PBM network and formulary decisions affect drug access and payments; concentrated local hospitals can negotiate higher insurer rates.
categories.whatBenefits: Dominant hospital systems, PBMs and affiliates may capture negotiation leverage, while some bargaining or scale economies lower selected prices.
categories.whoPays: Patients, payers, employers, independent pharmacies and medical practices can face restricted choices or higher rates.
categories.unresolved: No defensible average household PBM or hospital-concentration premium; plan design, insured versus uninsured status, local market and drug mix vary.

incomeExample.label: Pre-tax average income
incomeExample.comment: For job-market concentration, the measured issue is potential wage bargaining leverage; do not subtract income from expense categories to claim disposable income. BLS correlation is not a proven nationwide wage loss.

interpretationRules: Bar lengths represent BLS average spending amounts only—not concentration-attributable premiums.
Do not calculate overcharge dollars by multiplying household spending by market concentration percentages.
Never sum percentages with unrelated denominators or infer the share of a bill captured by a firm.
Housing includes utilities; do not double-count those amounts.
Food-at-home is a subset of food; label it precisely.
Household expenditure figures represent the BLS average consumer unit, not median local household spending.
Market case findings, allegations, regulated structures and observational studies must retain their original status.
No nationwide, ZIP-level or individual-household causal estimate is established.
Original Information is Beautiful graphics are linked for inspiration only; graphics and wording in Power Atlas are original.
These measured spending bars are not estimates of monopoly overcharges.
